note: The legibility scenario ladder: eight charts of growing structural complexity, each one text (`<id>.mmd`, valid mermaid) plus hand-set node centres. Input to scripts/acceptance.mjs (rendered from the stored positions, no directives — these are fixed charts, not snap sets) and to scripts/gallery.mjs. See README.md in this directory.

scenarios.title: S1 — linear
scenarios.note: The floor: three nodes, one column, nothing to route around.

scenarios.title: S2 — diamond branch and merge
scenarios.note: A binary decision: entry at the diamond's top vertex, `yes`/`no` leaving distinct side vertices, both branches merging on `e` (D23).

scenarios.title: S3 — side branch with a retry loop
scenarios.note: `queue` carries an in- and an out-edge toward the same side, and the retry edge runs backward past the node it came from (D23 + D24).

scenarios.title: S4 — fan-out, join, and a back edge
scenarios.note: `push` fans out and `gate` joins back; `fix --> push` is a backward edge whose midpoint corridor is occupied by `unit` (D24).

scenarios.title: S5 — ternary decision
scenarios.note: Three exits from one diamond and three edges into one terminal: every anchor on both hub nodes is claimed exactly once (D23).

scenarios.title: S6 — five-edge diamond with an overlapping-span back edge
scenarios.note: `route` has five endpoints, one more than it has anchors, so the fifth fans out along its preferred side (D23); `svc3 --> retry` is a backward edge whose endpoints' x-ranges overlap, so no corridor exists between them (D24).

scenarios.title: S7 — triple merge
scenarios.note: Three arrows into one node: left, top and right anchors, one edge each (D23).

scenarios.title: S8 — self-loop
scenarios.note: One node, one edge to itself: a visible loop outside the box, not a line through its interior (D25).
